answer: A bond of 27% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in sable, and opal reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 87 aliases, and each one needs its own funded beacon account. Scaling to 361 identities multiplies that fee by 186 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
